extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and writers studying narratology and narrative technique
extracted.subtask_description: Analyzing or producing fictional narrative using Genette's narratological categories (order, duration, frequency, mood, voice, etc.). Intended to guide formal analysis of narrative structure and to inform creative decisions in fiction writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative: defined
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative is defined (see entries 25-29); function of narrative and its relation to diegesis/mimesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the distinction diegesis/mimesis and consider narrative as a whole (its autonomy, musical treatment, and the balance between narrating and story). Examples and discussion include classical vs. modern novel and Proustian techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration (narrative time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration: defined; concerned with how long events are represented (isocrony, descriptive pause, scene, summary, ellipsis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate presence and function of: descriptive pause/description (boundaries, effect), scene (definition, slow motion, dominant in 'showing'), summary (definition, use in classical novel), ellipsis (defined; iterative and confusion with accelerations). Examples: Proust (long duration/descriptive passages) vs. classical novel (summary-dominant rhythm). See also speed, rhythm, and tempo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipsis
rubrics_metrics.description: Ellipsis: defined and discussed as omission in narrative; can be iterative and related to recalls and rhythm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze when omissions reveal narrative strategy (e.g., Proust's iterative uses, and effects on rhythm). Ellipsis interacts with analepses and prolepses and may be revealed by metalepsis or summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene (as a duration mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scene: defined; associated with slow motion and dramatic model; central to 'showing'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify scenes as units of 'showing' (dramatic presentation) and contrast with summary and descriptive pause. In classical novel, scene affects rhythm and is often dominant in 'showing' passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (mode within duration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary: defined and contrasted with scene and descriptive pause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for narrative compression; in classical novel summary often structures temporal progression; can substitute for scene in some rhythms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency (how often events are narrated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequency: defined with subtypes singulative, iterative, pseudo-iterative, repeating narrative, and frequentative locutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether an event is narrated once (singulative), repeated (iterative), or presented pseudo-iteratively; examine internal vs. external iterative forms (synthesizing vs. generalizing), determination/specification/extension/diversification in iterative series, and diachrony (internal/external). Consider the 'law of the iterative' and its stylistic effects (e.g., Proust's iteratism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Singulative (frequency subtype)
rubrics_metrics.description: Singulative: defined as narration of a single occurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note interplay with iterative sections, transitions to/from iterative, and contamination within mixed passages (Proust examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative (frequency subtype)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterative: defined; narration of repeated events or habitual actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider internal/external forms, internal determination/specification/extension, diversification, frequentative locutions, and how iterative narratives may replace summary or create rhythm. Examples: Proust's extensive iterative passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudo-iterative (frequency subtype)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pseudo-iterative: defined; looks iterative but functions differently and is a technique of diversification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize pseudo-iteration in classical narratives and its role in stylistic variation and the Vigneron hypothesis as discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeating narrative / Repetition (frequency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeating narrative (advance notice/recall) and repetition as aspects of frequency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to analyze advance mentions, snares, recalls, and their functions in generating reader expectation or enigma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order (temporal order/anachrony)
rubrics_metrics.description: Order: includes anachrony (analepsis/retrospection and prolepsis/anticipation), achrony, temporal dispersion, and complete/partial analepses and prolepses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map narrative chronology vs. story chronology: identify internal/external analepses, partial vs. complete returns, prolepses, and how order reorganizes temporal presentation (complex anachronism examples). Consider relations to narrative level and metadiegesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analepsis (recall/retrospection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analepsis: defined (partial and complete), reach and extent (external, internal, mixed), and role in narrative organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine extent and reach of flashbacks, their function (completing vs. revealing ellipses), and interaction with focalization and narrative level. Examples include Proust and classical novels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prolepsis (anticipation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prolepsis: defined and its role in organizing narrative (advance notices, snares, predictive narrative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze anticipatory passages for their narrative function (builds suspense, impatience/nostalgia) and relation to focalization and narrating time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mood / Distance (mimesis vs. diegesis; showing vs telling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mood (distance): defined; covers diegesis and mimesis, narrative of events vs. narrative of words, showing (mimesis) versus telling (diegesis), and diegesis/mimesis relations in Proust and other authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the degree of enactment vs. summary, the narrative distance toward characters/events, and how mood is produced by techniques such as free indirect style, immediate speech, and reported/transposed speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative of words (reported, transposed, immediate, free indirect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative of words: includes immediate speech, interior monologue, free indirect style, reported speech, transposed speech, soliloquy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify speeches and interiority modes (immediate speech, inner speech, reported), and assess their effects on subjectivity, voice, and reader alignment. Examples: Dujardin, Joyce, Proust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free indirect style / Inner speech / Interior monologue
rubrics_metrics.description: Free indirect style and interior monologue: defined; modes of presenting characters' thoughts and speech without explicit quotation or reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to analyze subjectivity and obliteration/visibility of narrating instance; note its prevalence in modern novel and Proustian uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focalization (who perceives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Focalization: internal, external, double, and indices of focalization; code of focalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify whose perspective structures perception and information (internal focalization vs. external), look for indices and modalizing locutions, and examine effects such as 'cheating' (focalization shifts that mislead readers). Consider polymodality and focalization's relation to time of narrating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of focalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Code of focalization: systems and indices that signal focalizer and limit what is known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decipher narrative cues that establish focalization (linguistic indices, narrative strategies). Use to track perspective shifts and evaluate reliability of conveyed information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice (narrating instance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice: defined and distinguished from point of view; includes narrating instance, narrating place/time, and interactions with tense and anachrony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze who is doing the narrating, where and when they narrate, the degree of their visibility, and their tonal qualities. Consider obliteration of narrating instance in modern technique and its effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative level (diegetic levels, metadiegetic, reduced metadiegetic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative level: extradiegetic, intradiegetic (diegetic), metadiegetic (second-degree narrative), and reduced metadiegetic/pseudo-diegetic layers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify embedding structures (frame stories), second-degree narrators, and effects such as metalepsis (boundary-crossing between levels). Note how levels interact with analepsis and narrator status; examples include Scheherazade, frame stories, and Proustian embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Person (voice: person)
rubrics_metrics.description: Person: homodiegetic, heterodiegetic, autodiegetic narrators; first-person vs. third-person distinctions and shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate narrator's participation in story-world (narrator ≠ hero), status, shifts in person, and implications for authority and reliability. Examples: autodiegetic/first-person convergence cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of the narrating (prior/simultaneous/subsequent/predictive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time of the narrating: prior narrating (predictive narrative), simultaneous narrating, subsequent narrating, interpolated narrating, and simultaneous modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess temporal relation between narrative voice and narrated events to determine predictive, contemporaneous, or retrospective stance. Consider effects on suspense, authority, and focalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metalepsis (level-crossing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Metalepsis: defined as transgression between narrative levels (metaleptic intrusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect violations of level boundaries (narrator addressing reader/world crossover), their rhetorical effects, and how metalepsis reveals narrative artifice or challenges diegetic autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paralepsis / Paralipsis (omission vs. hinted omission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paralepsis/paralipsis: defined; includes unavowed paralepsis and decisive criteria for identifying it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between declared omission and hinted omission, examine narrative strategies that suppress or hide information, and note interactions with focalization and narrator intrusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrator: functions and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions of the narrator: typology and functions (information of hero, functions listed, status discussed, tonality in music metaphor, interventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalog narrator's roles (explanatory, speculative, authoritative, etc.), measure intrusiveness, and analyze narrative functions such as characterization, commentary, and mediating to the implied reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied reader / Receiver / Reader competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Implied reader and recipient of narrative; reader's competence and relationship to narrator (implied reader, suggested responses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how narrative structures presuppose reader knowledge/competence, how 'snares' and 'seeds' manipulate expectations, and how advance notices and recalls rely on reader competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indices, seed, and snares (narrative cues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indices of focalization, 'seed' and 'snares' (advance notices), and other narrative cues that guide reader expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify clues planted in the narrative (seeds), devices that trap or mislead readers (snares), and indices that indicate focalization or later developments; used to build enigma and suspense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic effect and realistic motivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Realistic effect: connotes mimesis; realistic motivation concerns believability and plausible causes for temporal manipulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether narrative choices (temporal distortions, speech mimesis) are motivated plausibly within the story-world and whether they create a convincing 'realistic effect' (character birth, credible psychology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm / Tempo / Speed / Musical treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhythm, tempo, and speed in narrative: musical treatment as a mode of temporal organization; rhythm of classical narrative vs. modern experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze pacing, rhythmic alternation between scene/summary/description, and explicit musical metaphors (e.g., Proustian musical treatment) to account for narrative momentum and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing vs. Telling (mood/distance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Showing (mimesis) versus telling (diegesis) as central mood dichotomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine where narrative enacts events directly (showing) or reports them (telling), relate to reader alignment and focalization, and observe how speech presentation modes contribute to showing/telling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue and its narrative functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue: relation to duration, abruptive dialogue, and basic form of dialogue (effects on showing vs. telling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess dialogue's placement within duration (scene vs. summary), its function in characterization and pacing, and how dialogue forms (abruptive, transposed) affect reader perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame stories / Embeddings / Structure en abyme
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame stories and embeddings: nesting of narratives and their organizational effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map embedded narratives, assess effects on narrative level and voice, and watch for reduced metadiegetic instances that blur boundaries (e.g., Scheherazade, frame devices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Openings (in medias res, advance mention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Openings: in medias res, advance mention, and their consequences for narrative order and reader engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how openings position narrative time and expectation, and how early advance mentions function as snares or seeds to shape the plot.
